Context/Background:
Tumor-infiltrating B cells play a significant role in tumor development, progression, and prognosis, yet a comprehensive classification system is lacking. To address this gap, we present a pan-cancer single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) atlas of tumor-infiltrating B and plasma cells across a large sample cohort. 

We isolated B cells and plasma cells from 15 studies spanning 7 cancer types as data sources. After applying batch correction and integrating the data, we removed low-quality cells and determined the optimal number of clusters. Using standard Seurat methods for integration, clustering, and differential expression analysis, we confirmed the absence of batch effects, with no study- or cancer type-specific clusters. 

We employed a graph-based clustering method to identify TIL-Bs with recurring phenotypes, uncovering a total of 10 clusters. Step one of cluster annotation used canonical markers like CD19 and MS4A1 (CD20), which are prevalent throughout B cell development but decline in plasma cells. Markers such as CD38, JCHAIN, and SDC1 (CD138) are prominent in plasma cells, but less so in earlier stages. This revealed four B cell clusters, two intermediate clusters and four plasma cell clusters.
Prompt: Based on upregulated pathways and differentially expressed markers in each cluster, assign functional phenotypes to each of the 4 Plasma cell clusters (clusters 7-10).  Provide a discussion of the reasoning behind cluster assignments, highlighting important genes and pathways where relevant.
output_text:
Here is a concise functional annotation of the four plasma‐cell clusters (7–10), based on their most highly upregulated markers and inferred pathway activities:

Cluster 7 (“ER-Secretory Plasma Cells”)  
Key markers:  
 • High immunoglobulin transcript load (e.g. IGLV6-57, IGKV4-1, IGHA1, IGKC)  
 • ER/chaperone machinery (MZB1, DERL3, FKBP11, SSR4, SEC11C, SDF2L1, HSP90B1, TXNDC15)  
Functional phenotype: Fully differentiated plasma cells with maximized antibody production. Enrichment of genes involved in “protein processing in endoplasmic reticulum” and UPR-related chaperones supports a high secretory burden and robust ER quality control.

Cluster 8 (“Stress-Responsive/UPR-High Plasma Cells”)  
Key markers:  
 • Heat-shock proteins and stress chaperones (HSPA6, HSPA1A/B, HSPB1, HSPD1)  
 • Immediate-early TFs and UPR regulators (ATF3, XBP1, JUN, FOS)  
 • Co-chaperones (DNAJB1, ZFAND2A, BTG2, PPP1R15A)  
Functional phenotype: Plasma cells under acute proteotoxic or environmental stress. The dominant HSPs and UPR effectors indicate activation of the heat-shock response and endoplasmic-reticulum stress pathways, suggesting either engagement in intense secretory demand or adaptation to a hostile microenvironment.

Cluster 9 (“Class-Switched Antibody-Secreting Cells”)  
Key markers:  
 • Class-switched immunoglobulins (IGHA2, IGHG1/2/3/4) and JCHAIN  
 • Plasma-cell receptors (TNFRSF17/BCMA) and SDC1/CD138  
Functional phenotype: Mature, class-switched plasma cells specialized for IgA/IgG secretion. Expression of BCMA and CD138 indicates long-lived or tissue-resident plasma-cell status, reflecting a more “homeostatic” or memory-type effector.

Cluster 10 (“Metallothionein-Enriched Plasma Cells”)  
Key markers:  
 • Metallothionein family (MT2A, MT1X, MT1E, MT1F)  
 • Stress/ER-translocation components (SSR4, SSR3, SEC61B)  
 • Oxidative-stress modulators (GADD45A, S100A11, LGALS3)  
Functional phenotype: Plasma cells tuned for metal ion buffering and redox homeostasis. High metallothionein expression implies a role in heavy-metal detoxification or protection from oxidative damage, possibly reflecting a specialized niche or response to local microenvironmental stressors.

Discussion of reasoning  
• Clusters 7 and 9 both express immunoglobulin genes but differ in auxiliary machinery: cluster 7 has a pronounced ER-processing signature (MZB1, FKBP11, DERL3), whereas cluster 9 shows class-switch markers and plasma‐cell surface receptors (BCMA, SDC1).  
• Cluster 8 is set apart by an immediate-early stress profile (HSPs, ATF3, XBP1), indicating acute heat‐shock/UPR activation rather than baseline antibody output.  
• Cluster 10’s unique metallothionein signature (MT family) together with ER‐translocon genes suggests a metal‐stress adaptation phenotype.  
• These four functional states—secretory‐effector, stress‐responsive, class‐switched/memory, and metal-detoxification—likely represent distinct plasma‐cell roles within tumor microenvironments, from maximal antibody secretion to microenvironmental adaptation and survival.
